paper_findings: syracuse.tex:55 — the two cases of f_A are swapped: as printed f_A(x) = 3x+1 for x ∈ 2A and x/2 for x ∉ 2A, but x/2 does not exist for x ∉ 2A, so no such map exists in any Z/2Z-ring (Syracuse.printed_f_not_definable, at x = 1). The formalized f halves on 2A and sends x ↦ 3x+1 off 2A, as in the integer definition l.46–48.

syracuse.tex:55 — T_A(x) = (3x+1)/2^{nu_2(3x+1)} is undefined at x0 = -1/3 whenever 3 is a unit of A (Z_2 = the 2-adic integers, also Z/2Z; Z_(2) and Z[1/3] are further examples, not formalized here): x0 ∈ 2A+1, 3x0+1 = 0, {n | 0 ∈ 2^n A} has no max, and (when 2 ≠ 0) no odd t and k ∈ N satisfy 2^k t = 3x0+1 (Syracuse.T_undefined_of_isUnit_three; in Z_2: Syracuse.T_undefined_padicInt). It is the only defect: 3x+1 = 0 forces 3 ∈ A^× (Syracuse.three_mul_add_one_ne_zero), so over Z every point is good. Where 3x+1 ≠ 0, T x is odd, 2^{nu_2(3x+1)} T x = 3x+1, and it is the unique such odd element (T_odd, pow_v2_mul_T, T_unique).

syracuse.tex:50 — 'in such a ring, 2 ≠ 0' is false for A = Z/2Z itself, which is integral, noetherian and has A/2A = A ≅ Z/2Z (Syracuse.instIsZ2RingZMod2, Syracuse.two_eq_zero_zmod2). It is the only exception: in a Z/2Z-ring, 2 = 0 iff A ≅ Z/2Z (Syracuse.IsZ2Ring.two_eq_zero_iff). There halves are not unique; and if 'such a ring' in the last sentence of l.50 means any Z/2Z-ring (it may mean only the rings named just before it, which have characteristic 0), '4 ≠ 0' fails for Z/2Z too; with 2 ≠ 0 the ring has characteristic 0 (Syracuse.IsZ2Ring.charZero_of_two_ne_zero). The claim A_2 ≅ Z_2 (l.52) also fails for Z/2Z (not formalized here; it belongs to T-syr-rep).

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:67–68 — as printed the lemma covers x0 = -1/3 when 3 ∈ A^×, where T_A(x0) and p_1(x0) do not exist; no assignment of an odd value t to T_A(x0) and of k ∈ N to p_1(x0) satisfies the n = 1 instance 2^k t - 3x0 = 1 (Syracuse.base_printed_fails_padicInt, in Z_2). The strongest true form is proved: the identity holds for every x ∈ A and n for the total maps (Syracuse.base), and on every orbit avoiding -1/3 all its terms are the paper's (Syracuse.base_of_orbit), hence for all x when 3 ∉ A^×, in particular in Z (Syracuse.base_of_not_isUnit_three).
syracuse.tex:71 and 75 — the proof writes a_1(x) for nu_2(3x+1); by def:ring_define_2 (l.62–63) this is a_0(x) = p_1(x), and p_{n+1}(x) = a_0(x) + p_n(T_A x).

syracuse.tex:75–77 — the last sums of the proof have shifted indices: Σ_{k=1}^{n} 2^{p_{k+1}(x)} 3^{n-1-k} should read Σ_{k=1}^{n} 2^{p_k(x)} 3^{n-k} (the exponent n-1-k is negative at k = n), and the final Σ_{k=0}^{n} 2^{p_{k+1}(x)} 3^{n-1-k} should read Σ_{k=0}^{n} 2^{p_k(x)} 3^{n-k}, the statement at n+1. The statement itself is correct.

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:84–86 — false as printed: in the Z/2Z-ring Z/2Z, RHS_2(0,1) = 3+2 = 1 = 3+4 = RHS_2(0,2) (Syracuse.ring_maps_rhs_printed_false); RHS_n is not injective for every n ≥ 2 (Syracuse.rhs_zmod2_not_injOn; it is in fact constant, = 3^{n-1} = 1, but only non-injectivity is proved); the printed universal statement is refuted (Syracuse.ring_maps_rhs_printed_statement_false). It holds whenever 2 ≠ 0 (Syracuse.ring_maps_rhs), i.e. for every Z/2Z-ring other than Z/2Z, and then without p_0 = 0 (Syracuse.rhs_injOn_strictMono). The paper prints no proof; the one here peels off the 2-adic valuation p_0 of RHS_n(p) = 2^{p_0}·(odd) and inducts on n. Under the printed definition (l.52, without the integrality of l.50) it also fails for rings with 2 ≠ 0: ZMod 6, RHS_2(0,1) = 5 = 11 = RHS_2(0,3) (Syracuse.rhs_zmod6_not_injOn).

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:88–90 — false as printed on 2A_2+1 = 2Z_2+1: x0 = -1/3 is odd but not in the image of the printed inverse φ^{-1} (Syracuse.neg_inv3_not_mem_image), nor is any y_k = -(2^k+3)/9, k ≥ 1, which satisfies T(y_k) = -1/3 with ν_2(3y_k+1) = k (Syracuse.neg_third_preimage). Hence no map φ from 2Z_2+1 to {p | p_0 = 0, p ↗↗} has the printed φ^{-1} as a left inverse, whatever values are given to the undefined p_n on the backward orbit of -1/3 (Syracuse.rep_printed_false). Strongest true form proved (Syracuse.theo_rep): φ: x ↦ (p_n(x)) is a bijection from RepDomain (odd x whose T-orbit avoids -1/3) onto the strictly increasing sequences from 0, its inverse is the printed formula, and the image of the formula is exactly RepDomain (Syracuse.repInv_image). This is the theorem-level form of OQ-42 (d).

syracuse.tex:92–95 — the proof establishes only φ^{-1} ∘ φ = id (x = -(1/3)Σ 2^{p_k(x)}/3^k, i.e. injectivity of φ); that every strictly increasing p with p_0 = 0 is some φ(x) (surjectivity, and that the printed formula lands in the domain) is not argued. It is proved here: S(q) = Σ 2^{q_n}/3^n satisfies S(q) = 1 + (1/3)2^{q_1}S(q') with q'_n = q_{n+1} - q_1 (Syracuse.repSeries_eq), so 3φ^{-1}(q)+1 = 2^{q_1}φ^{-1}(q') with φ^{-1}(q') odd, whence T(φ^{-1}q) = φ^{-1}q' and a_0(φ^{-1}q) = q_1 (Syracuse.T_repInv) and p_n(φ^{-1}q) = q_n (Syracuse.rep_repInv). The proof's displayed identity (l.93) also writes x ∈ 2A+1 where 2A_2+1 is meant, and holds only on orbits avoiding -1/3.

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:108 — false as printed: '∀ i, j ∈ ⟦1, n⟧' includes i = j, where A_i^n(a(x)) - A_j^n(a(x)) = 0, on every cycle; e.g. the cycle (1) of Z, n = 1, i = j = 1 (Syracuse.cor_ring_periodic_minimal_period_printed_false). For i ≠ j it holds in every Z/2Z-ring, with no 2 ≠ 0 (Syracuse.Aun_sub_ne_zero), for the printed A_u^n and for the off-by-one reading of OQ-43 (Syracuse.AunAlt_sub_ne_zero). Proof (the paper prints none): with x_u = T^u(x), on any orbit A_u^n(a(x)) = 2^{p_n(x_u)}(3x_{u+n}+1) - 3^n(3x_u+1) (Syracuse.Aun_cast_eq, from lem:base at n+1), so on a cycle A_u^n = (2^{p_n} - 3^n)(3x_u+1) as printed and (2^{p_n} - 3^n)x_u with the product to n-2-k (Syracuse.Aun_cast_of_cycle); 2^{p_n} - 3^n is odd since p_n ≥ 1 on a cycle, and x_1, ..., x_n are distinct by minimality. The corrected form is not vacuous: the cycle (-5, -7) of Z has least period 2 (Syracuse.cycle_neg_five).

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:114 — the statement holds as printed (Syracuse.one_has), and in the sharper form p_n(x) log 2 − n log 3 ≤ n log(1 + 1/(3|x|)) for every x ∈ Z*, either sign (Syracuse.one_has_sharp); the hypothesis is needed only for k ≤ n (Syracuse.one_has_of_le). The proof used is the product form of lem:base, 2^{p_n(x)} T^n(x) = 3^n x Π_{k<n}(1 + 1/(3T^k(x))) (Syracuse.pow_p_mul_T_iterate_eq_prod), in place of the Grönwall step.

syracuse.tex:119 — the displayed equation drops the factor 1/3 that dividing lem:base by 3^n produces (the right side should be (1/3) Σ_{k<n} e^{p_k log 2 − k log 3}); as printed it is false at x = 1, n = 1, where the left side is 4/3 − 1 = 1/3 and the right side is 1 (Syracuse.one_has_proof_l119_false). Harmless: dropping 1/3 only weakens the inequality of l.121.
syracuse.tex:123 — u_k is defined as exp(log(2) p_k(x) − n log(3)); k log(3) is meant.

syracuse.tex:124 — the bound (1 + 1/x)^n should read (1 + 1/|x|)^n, as in the statement: as printed it is false at x = −1, n = 1, which satisfies the hypothesis (T(−1) = −1) and has e^{p_1 log 2 − log 3} = 2/3 > 0 = 1 + 1/(−1) (Syracuse.one_has_proof_l124_false).

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:130–131 — the first bullet is false at n = 0 for every x ∈ N*: T^0(x) = x ≤ x and it asks p_0(x) log 2 − 0 = 0 > 0 (Syracuse.itemize_first_fails_at_zero, Syracuse.itemize_first_printed_false). It holds for every n ≥ 1 (Syracuse.itemize_first).

syracuse.tex:132 — the second bullet is false at x = 1 for every n ≥ 1: T(1) = 1, a_k(1) = 2, p_n(1) = 2n (Syracuse.T_one_int, Syracuse.a_one_int, Syracuse.p_one_int), so p_n(1) log 2 − n log 3 = n log(4/3) < n log 2 = n log(1 + 1/1) (Syracuse.itemize_second_fails_at_one, Syracuse.itemize_second_printed_false). The true bound is n log(1 + 1/(3x)) (Syracuse.itemize_second, hypothesis needed only for k ≤ n), attained at x = 1 for every n (Syracuse.itemize_second_sharp), so the constant 1/3 is sharp. 'Proceed the same way' (l.138): the same product identity gives it, with the inequalities reversed.
syracuse.tex:132 — whether the printed bound n log(1 + 1/x) holds for every x ≥ 2 is not decided here (it bears on hypothetical positive cycles).

paper_findings: syracuse.tex:140 — the corollary has no printed proof; it holds as printed (Syracuse.corollary_2). Proof: by the product form, p_n(x) log 2 − n log 3 = log|x| − log|T^n x| + Σ_{k<n} log(1 + 1/(3T^k x)); the first difference is eventually ≤ 0, and the Cesàro mean of log(1 + 1/(3T^k x)) ≤ 1/(3T^k x) → 0 tends to 0 (Syracuse.corollary_2_eventually).

statements.blocked_on: OQ-54 (c) (the corrected form: bounds swapped, with the factor 3)
paper_findings: syracuse.tex:142 — false as printed: at x = 1, n = 1 (min = max = 1, p_1(1) = 2) it asks log_2 2 = 1 ≤ 2 − log_2 3 ≈ 0.415 (Syracuse.bounds_printed_false). More: its lower bound log_2(1 + 1/min) fails on every positive cycle (Syracuse.bounds_printed_lower_false), and its two bounds are in decreasing order (1/min ≥ 1/max), so the printed chain could only hold on a fixed point.

syracuse.tex:142 — the true form (no printed proof): on every cycle of Z* (either sign), p_n/n − log_2 3 = (1/n) Σ_{k<n} log_2(1 + 1/(3T^k x)) (Syracuse.cycle_mean), hence log_2(1 + 1/(3 max)) ≤ p_n/n − log_2 3 ≤ log_2(1 + 1/(3 min)) (Syracuse.bounds): the printed bounds are swapped and lack the factor 3. On a negative cycle both bounds are negative.
